title: A Phone Call About Forgiving a Business Partner
script: Farah: [tense] Bagas, I need to talk to you about the money you were supposed to invest in our shop last month. It still hasn't arrived.
Bagas: [nervous] I know, Farah, and I'm sorry. Things happened that I didn't expect, and I should have called you sooner to explain everything.
Farah: Because of that delay, I had to borrow money from my brother just to pay our supplier on time.
Bagas: [ashamed] I feel terrible hearing that. I promised you that money would come through, and instead I put you in a difficult position.
Farah: What actually happened, Bagas? You've always been reliable before this, so I'm confused about what changed.
Bagas: [honestly] My father got sick suddenly, and the hospital bills used almost everything I had saved for the shop this year.
Farah: [softening] Why didn't you just tell me that immediately, instead of staying quiet and letting me wonder what was going on?
Bagas: I was embarrassed, honestly. I didn't want you to think I couldn't handle both my family and our business at the same time.
Farah: [hurt] I would have understood completely if you had just explained it. Silence was what actually hurt more than the missing money did.
Bagas: You're right. I should have trusted you with the truth instead of avoiding your calls for almost two weeks.
Farah: [compassionately] I understand why you used your own savings for your father. But our business still needs a clear revised plan because I made commitments based on your promise.
Bagas: Thank you for saying that. I was afraid you would end our partnership over this.
Farah: [firmly] I was hurt, but I'm not going to throw away three years of trust because of one difficult month.
Bagas: [carefully] I can confirm a safe amount by Friday. Then we should write a revised schedule based on my actual finances, not on when my father recovers.
Farah: Let us review the supplier debt and put the new agreement in writing. And please talk to me early next time, instead of disappearing when things get hard.
Bagas: [sincerely] I promise. And thank you for forgiving me, even though I honestly didn't handle this well at all.
Farah: [hopeful] Everyone struggles sometimes, Bagas. What matters now is that we keep building this shop together, honestly, from here forward.

quiz.question: Why does Farah call Bagas at the start?
options: Because the money he promised to invest never arrived
To end their friendship
To ask him to work longer hours
To plan a trip
quiz.explanation: Farah calls because the money Bagas was supposed to invest in their shop last month still hasn't arrived.

quiz.question: What actually happened to Bagas's money?
options: He lost it gambling
He spent it on a vacation
His father got sick, and hospital bills used his savings
He gave it to another business
quiz.explanation: Bagas's father got sick suddenly, and the hospital bills used almost everything he had saved.

quiz.question: Why didn't Bagas tell Farah sooner?
options: He forgot
He was embarrassed and didn't want her to think he couldn't handle everything
He was too busy to call
He didn't have her number
quiz.explanation: Bagas admits he was embarrassed and didn't want Farah to think he couldn't handle his family and the business.

quiz.question: What does Farah say hurt her more than the missing money?
options: The amount of money itself
Losing the shop
Borrowing from her brother
Bagas's silence and avoiding her calls
quiz.explanation: Farah says silence was what actually hurt more than the missing money.

quiz.question: What does Farah decide about their partnership?
options: She ends it immediately
She forgives him and wants to keep building the shop together
She demands all the money at once
She asks someone else to be her partner
quiz.explanation: Farah decides not to throw away three years of trust and wants to keep building the shop together.

quiz.question: What practical harm did the silence cause Farah?
options: She closed the shop immediately
She borrowed money to pay the supplier
She paid the hospital bill
She lost contact with her brother
quiz.explanation: Farah made an expensive adjustment without information.

quiz.question: Why is Farah’s revised response both kind and responsible?
options: She cancels the entire debt
She respects the family need but still requires a business plan
She ignores the supplier commitment
She demands money during the call
quiz.explanation: Compassion does not erase commitments made to the shop.

quiz.question: Why should repayment not depend on the father’s recovery?
options: Recovery time is uncertain and should not become a financial promise
The father caused the partnership problem
Hospital care always ends by Friday
Farah controls the recovery date
quiz.explanation: A responsible schedule uses finances that can actually be checked.

quiz.question: What does putting the agreement in writing achieve?
options: It publicly exposes the father’s illness
It guarantees the shop will succeed
It creates shared expectations that both partners can review
It removes the need for future communication
quiz.explanation: A written repair makes dates and responsibilities clear.

quiz.question: What must accompany Farah’s forgiveness?
options: No further discussion of money
A promise that hardship will not return
Ending the partnership immediately
Earlier honesty and reliable follow-through
quiz.explanation: Trust can continue, but it needs changed behavior and accountability.
